items.title: Brij Bhushan acquittal: What the order leaves open to scrutiny
items.summary: On August 3, 2026, a Delhi trial court acquitted Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, the former Wrestling Federation of India president, of charges under Sections 354, 354A, and 506(I) of the Indian Penal Code in the sexual harassment case brought by six women wrestlers. Vinod Tomar, the WFI’s former assistant secretary, was acquitted of the remaining charge against him. The court held that the prosecution had failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. That conclusion is not, by itself, unusual. Criminal courts are required to acquit where the prosecution evidence leaves a reasonable doubt. What deserves closer examination is the route this particular judgment took to get there. The case so far The allegations went back to January 2023, when some of India’s most decorated wrestlers, including Vinesh Phogat, Sakshi Malik, and Bajrang Punia, sat down in protest at Jantar Mantar, accusing Singh of sexually harassing junior wrestlers over several years, at training camps, tournaments, and federation events. Singh, then a six-time BJP MP, denied everything and dared the wrestlers to prove it in court. It took months of protest, and a nudge from the Supreme Court, before Delhi Police registered two separate FIRs against Singh in April 2023 – one under the IPC for the adult complainants, and a second under the POCSO Act for the seventh, minor complainant. The POCSO case never made it to trial: the minor later withdrew her allegations, police filed a cancellation report, and the case was formally closed in May 2025. The IPC case, brought by the six adult complainants, is the one that reached trial. A chargesheet followed in June 2023, and in May 2024 a magistrate ordered charges framed against Singh under Sections 354, 354A, 354D, and 506 IPC. That trial ran for more than two years, held partly in camera, before Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate (ACJM) Ashwani Panwar delivered the acquittal on August 3. Two complainants had turned hostile at trial, telling the court they had been “forced” or “pressured” into making the allegations. items.title: Stop asking whether arbitration is dead, start asking why it isn't delivering
items.summary: In conversations around endless events, panel discussions, fireside chats and the like, ‘experts’ promote arbitration as the most effective method of dispute resolution in the commercial space. Water cooler tete-a-tete, however, tells us a different story. A chat with a General Counsel of any respectable multinational will disclose a disquiet about the increasing costs, delays and unpredictability normally associated with arbitration in India. Thus, the real question to address is why the system, as it currently stands, is not consistently delivering on its promise within the Indian context. Recent remarks have brought this debate into sharp focus. On the one hand, there are concerns that aspects of the current arbitral framework may be undermining its effectiveness. On the other, there is a strong and concurrent recognition of the tremendous scope of arbitration and mediation in the light of mounting pendency before courts . This apparent paradox is significant. It reflects not a system in decline, but one at a crossroads: simultaneously critiqued for its shortcomings while at the same time seen as an essential solution to endemic judicial burdens. Against this backdrop, this article does not subscribe to the alarmist call to move away from arbitration in India. To do so is both puerile and misdirected. The pertinent question to ask is why arbitration is not consistently delivering on its foundational promise of cost effectiveness, efficiency, finality and party autonomy within the Indian context. This shift in perspective is not merely semantic; it fundamentally alters the narrative. It moves the discourse away from abandoning arbitration as an alternative dispute resolution mechanism and instead directs attention towards diagnosing the structural, procedural and institutional challenges that hinder its effective functioning. Importantly, these concerns are not unique to India. Mature arbitration hubs such as Singapore, London, Paris and New York continue to grapple with recurring criticisms relating to rising costs, procedural delays, the quality and consistency of arbitrators, enforceability concerns, and questions of overall efficiency. Yet, none of these jurisdictions have concluded that arbitration is a lost cause. Instead, they have responded through continuous refinement of rules, building institutional support and nuanced practices. items.title: Karnataka High Court stays case against student booked for throwing eggs at BJP MLA amid protest
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Friday stayed criminal proceedings against an engineering student booked in a criminal case on allegations that he was among those who threw eggs at Bharitiya Janata Party (BJP) MLA BP Harish amid NEET-related protests. Justice M Nagaprasanna passed the interim order staying further proceedings in the criminal case filed against the student. Justice M Nagaprasanna The incident occured outside the Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) office in Bengaluru last month. Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) BP Harish had arrived at the site to attend a protest organised by the BJP to oppose the demonstration led by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi in Delhi outside Prime Minister Modi's residence over national exam paper leaks. However, unknown to Harish, the remaining BJP leaders who had planned to participate in the protest were reportedly detained by the police en route, leaving him alone outside the KPCC office where Congress workers were waiting to rally against the BJP. As Harish was being escorted away by the police, eggs were hurled at him. Nine persons were booked in the criminal case registered consequently on the BJP leader's complaint, including an engineering student named Punya C Naik. The case cites the offences under Sections 115(2) (hurt), 118(1) (hurt by dangerous weapons or means), 126(2) (wrongful restraint), and 190 (unlawful assembly) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS). Naik eventually moved the High Court with a plea to quash the criminal case. His counsel contended that the case was filed under political pressure and that Naik was picked up at random from the street among other students who were rounded up by the police. Advocate Shathabish Shivanna maintained that the student had only arrived at the site to peacefully protest against the alleged police brutality that took place in Delhi's Jantar Mantar amid student protests about NEET/ exam paper leaks. He asserted that the student had not attacked anyone. After considering these preliminary submissions, the Court sought the State's response and granted the student interim relief by staying criminal proceedings against him. Advocates Rithvik Balanagraj B and Milton Herburt MM also appeared for the student.

items.title: SCBA urges Meghalaya bar bodies to withdraw resolution against Advocate General Amit Kumar
items.summary: The Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) has urged the Meghalaya High Court Bar Association and the Shillong Bar Association to reconsider and withdraw their joint resolution seeking action against Meghalaya Advocate General Amit Kumar . The SCBA said the resolution, passed in the context of Kumar’s submissions before the Meghalaya High Court on the safety and dignity of women advocates and law interns, was unwarranted since the issue was already being considered by the Court. The statement came after the two Meghalaya bar associations passed a joint resolution on Thursday expelling Kumar from their rolls and calling for his removal as Advocate General. The associations had taken exception to his alleged remarks that bar associations had failed to provide a safe environment for women lawyers. The SCBA, however, said the context in which the remarks were made needed to be taken into account. It noted that Kumar, while appearing as Advocate General, had informed the Meghalaya High Court about the action taken in the case and submitted that while the safety of members of the bar must be protected, equal attention must be given to the safety and dignity of women advocates and law interns. The SCBA said that since these submissions were made during judicial proceedings in a matter already before the Meghalaya High Court, seeking action against the Advocate General for those submissions was unwarranted. The association also expressed concern that the resolution could further escalate the controversy. The SCBA has therefore urged the concerned bar associations to withdraw the resolution and instead work towards an effective and confidential mechanism through which women advocates and law interns can raise grievances and seek redressal. It said the safety and dignity of every member of the legal profession must remain a collective responsibility of the Bar. The controversy arose during proceedings before the Meghalaya High Court concerning the alleged physical assault and public parading of an advocate in Shillong. The advocate had earlier been accused of molesting a law intern. During the proceedings, the High Court also expressed concern over the failure of the police to act despite being present when the incident occurred. The bar associations subsequently approached the High Court, raising concerns over the incident and the safety of lawyers. The matter later led to the Advocate General’s submissions concerning the need to protect women advocates and interns.

items.title: A river became a deity and a person between two hearings: Tamirabarani and the turn to spiritual ecology
items.summary: On July 23, 2026, the Madras High Court in Sivanupandian v. District Collector did something interesting. It recognised the personhood of the Tamirabarani River, as it is worshipped as a deity in the Hindu faith. The Court accordingly held that no one had a right to pollute the River. Such pollution, the Court said, would not only breach environmental statutes and the fundamental rights of citizens under Article 21 of the Constitution, but would also violate the rights of the River herself, recognised for her intrinsic value. The Court clarified that juristic personality was being conferred only for a limited purpose: the River’s right not to be polluted. The significance of the decision lies not merely in the recognition of legal personality, but in the route adopted by the Court. It used personhood to perform an expressive function. The law was invoked not only to prohibit an act, but also to change the perception and moral description of that act. From an eviction dispute to a larger environmental question The petitioner before the High Court was aggrieved by an eviction order passed under Section 6 of the Land Encroachment Act, 1905 , directing him to vacate the Anandavilas Mandapam in Tirunelveli District. The technical challenge and the petitioner’s individual claim are not especially relevant for present purposes. The Court itself noted that the writ petition might not be maintainable. But the Court did not give the matter a quietus merely by sustaining the eviction order. The proceedings assumed a wider environmental dimension when the Court was informed that thousands of devotees ordinarily visited the bathing ghats of the Tamirabarani River. On certain occasions, devotees gathered in large numbers to pay homage to their deceased ancestors. The associated rituals involved the discarding of used and unused garments, towels, clothes, slippers and other articles connected with the deceased. The issue was particularly serious because the Tamirabarani is a perennial river catering to the drinking-water needs of crores of people. items.title: Protect interests of students: Supreme Court asks CBSE to address OSM evaluation issues
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday asked the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) to explore ways to protect the interests of students facing difficulties in entrance-based admissions due to their scores under the Board’s new On-Screen Marking (OSM) system for evaluating answer sheets. A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was told that some students had cleared their CBSE examinations and had subsequently appeared for entrance examinations for other courses. However, they had not secured the minimum marks required for admission because of their CBSE scores, and some of the courses had already commenced. The plea linked the lesser marks/ scores to the irregularities in OSM evaluation system. According to the petition, CBSE issued a circular on February 9, 2026 regarding the OSM system and another circular on the same day concerning the relieving of teachers for the entire day to undertake evaluation through the system. A further circular issued on February 14 dealt with updating teachers’ personal credentials and login guidelines, while a February 18 communication directed teachers to complete mock evaluations and monitoring exercises as part of the OSM training process. The petitioner, however, alleged that no official training was provided to the concerned teachers for examination and evaluation through the OSM system and that the system was implemented without adequate formal information or training. items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently observed that addressing a wife as “barren woman” may not constitute cruelty under Section 498-A of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) when there is exchange of “filthy verbal blows” from both sides. Justice Indrajeet Shukla was dealing with a man’s petition challenging a Lucknow court order summoning him in a complaint filed by his wife over alleged cruelty, dowry demand and intentional insult. “In the case in hand, the entire version of complainant if tested on the touchstone of legal requirements, for even prima facie constituting the offence of cruelty, the address as ‘barren woman’ could not be termed as cruelty, particularly when there are exchange of filthy verbal blows from both the sides,” the Court said. Justice Indrajeet Shukla Allahabad High Court The address as ‘barren woman’ could not be termed as cruelty, particularly when there are exchange of filthy verbal blows from both the sides. It noted that the wife herself had called the husband “impotent” when she was addressed as “barren woman” by him and his relatives. It added that the allegation of calling the complainant a ‘barren woman’ is undoubtedly insensitive and reprehensible but in the present case, such utterance did not satisfy the ingredients of intentional insult with intent or knowledge to provoke a breach of the peace to attract Section 504 IPC. items.title: Supreme Court allows declaration of results of Delhi Bar Council polls results subject to election tribunal decisions

A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said that election disputes should be raised before the tribunals already constituted to adjudicate such matters. The Court also requested the tribunals to decide the disputes expeditiously, preferably within 3 months. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana The Bench noted that several petitions concerning irregularities in different state bar council elections had been brought before the Supreme Court. Since the Court had already constituted election tribunals headed by former judges to deal with such disputes, it said that there was no reason to adopt a different approach in the case of the BCD elections. It accordingly disposed of the petitions, granting aggrieved parties liberty to approach the election tribunals. The Bench made it clear that the results of the BCD elections could be declared, but would remain subject to the outcome of the pending disputes. It also directed the BCD to preserve the entire election record. The Delhi Police was directed to preserve the original CCTV footage relating to the election process and provide copies to the concerned parties, so that the material remains available for consideration by the tribunals. The Supreme Court had earlier permitted counting of the votes polled in the BCD elections to continue, while directing that the results could not be declared without its permission. The elections had been followed by allegations of irregularities in the counting process. During the proceedings, counsel appearing before the Supreme Court raised allegations of tampering with ballot papers and excess votes. Senior Advocate Vikas Singh submitted that the BCD had a 5-year term which had continued for 8 years and urged that the election results be declared. He also referred to allegations that thousands of votes had been tampered with. The Bench, however, said that such issues could be raised before the election tribunal. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday asked rival groups in Manipur to work towards a comprehensive proposal to reopen national highways blocked amid fresh Naga-Kuki confrontations. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana observed that the continuing blockades were hurting ordinary people and disrupting the supply of essential commodities. The Court urged the rival sides to look beyond the immediate dispute and find a mechanism to reopen the routes. “Blocking of highways is not serving anybody’s cause. Hardship is faced by everyone. Why don’t you consider the intervention of some agency, SLA (service-level agreement), or any other platform. You must be tired of this fighting,” said the Court. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana The Court was hearing a fresh plea by the Kuki Women Organisation for Human Rights (KWOHR) seeking the removal of a blockade on National Highway-2 (NH-2) and restoration of supplies to Kuki-dominated areas. NH-2, which connects Imphal with Dimapur in Nagaland, is one of the State's principal supply routes. Along with NH-37, which connects Imphal with Jiribam and onward to Assam, it is a crucial route for bringing goods into the landlocked State. The present dispute over the highways stems from a fresh Naga-Kuki confrontation that erupted in May this year, with the two communities accusing armed groups from the other side of abducting their members. According to news reports , on May 13, several civilians were abducted in the Kangpokpi and Senapati districts after a series of attacks. While many were subsequently released, six Naga men remained unaccounted for. Fourteen Kuki civilians were also held captive by Naga groups before being released in June. items.title: Understanding the intelligence pyramid: Why most businesses know everything and do nothing?
items.summary: In every consequential field of human endeavour, whether in the boardroom, the courtroom, or on the trading floor, one resource has consistently separated those who prevail from those who do not. The resource is intelligence: information that has been processed, placed in context, and converted into a decision within the window in which that decision still counts. Military history makes the point plainly. The intelligence failures that determined the outcomes of wars were rarely failures of collection; the signals were usually present. What failed was the architecture to convert those signals into understanding, and the discipline to act before the moment passed. Corporate history repeats the lesson, and increasingly, so does the law. When a regulator, a court, or a shareholder examines how an organisation behaved before a loss crystallised, the question is seldom whether the information existed. It is whether the organisation recognised what it held and converted that knowledge into a reasoned, recorded decision, or allowed it to travel no further than the report in which it arrived. In India, Section 166 of the Companies Act, 2013 requires directors to act in good faith and to exercise due and reasonable care, skill, and diligence, a standard against which a board's conduct is later assessed with the benefit of hindsight. This framing is more instructive. And it is the framing of the Intelligence Pyramid , a framework developed by IIRIS, that is designed to address. Directors' duties and the architecture of decision-making The Intelligence Pyramid categorizes enterprise intelligence into three levels: Strategic, Tactical, and Operational . The basic principle behind the intelligence pyramid is that intelligence needs to flow continuously and bidirectionally through all three levels. The minute that process gets broken down due to departmental silos, conflicting incentives, or poor infrastructure, it is not just an issue of becoming less responsive but one of creating liabilities. It encompasses domains such as Regulatory and Compliance Foresight, M&A and Strategic Alliance Intelligence, and Insider Threat Intelligence. items.title: Chandigarh court directs Meta to remove AI-generated video of Punjab MLA Sukhpal Khaira
items.summary: A Chandigarh court has directed Meta platforms to remove from Facebook and Instagram a morphed and artificial intelligence-generated video depicting Punjab MLA Sukhpal Singh Khaira in an off-shoulder women’s dress. Civil Judge (Junior Division) Kaushal Kumar Yadav passed the ad interim order on August 12 after finding that Khaira had made out a prima facie case for an injunction. “ The content uploaded is apparently defamatory, objectionable and AI generated, ” the Court said. The Court added that Khaira would suffer irreparable loss and injury if the content continued to remain accessible and circulate on public platforms. The court directed Meta, its agents and representatives to disable access to the identified video and posts uploaded on the Facebook page “Charda Punjab” and Instagram account “Chard_apunjab”. The content and identified URLs must be removed within 72 hours of Meta receiving the order, the Court directed. Khaira, who represents the Bholath constituency in the Punjab Legislative Assembly, filed the suit seeking permanent and mandatory injunctions, protection of his reputation, dignity and personality rights. According to the suit, the operators of the accounts circulated a digitally manipulated video in which Khaira’s recognisable face, beard and turbaned Sikh appearance were superimposed on an artificially generated body wearing an off-shoulder women’s dress. Khaira claimed that the video had been widely circulated and damaged his reputation globally. His counsel also highlighted objections raised over the use of his turbaned Sikh appearance. Since the identities and addresses of the account operators were unknown, Khaira impleaded them as Ashok Kumar or John Doe defendants (unknown entities). He also sought a direction to Meta to disclose their basic subscriber information Meta submitted that it was an intermediary with no personal knowledge of the content and would comply with the court’s directions. While granting the interim takedown relief, the court did not expressly allow the request for subscriber information. The matter will be heard next on September 14. Advocate Sarabjot Singh Cheema represented Khaira. Advocate Abhijeet Singh Rawaley appeared for Meta. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday upheld the life sentence of a man convicted of murdering a woman over allegations that she practised witchcraft. [ Balku Oram v. State of Odisha ] A Bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and NV Anjaria held that the trial court and the Orissa High Court had correctly held the accused guilty and that his conviction and sentence deserved to be affirmed. The Court said the direct evidence on record clearly established the role of the accused and the co-accused in the killing. "The nature of the direct evidence appearing against the appellant (Balku Oram) is compelling, which clearly establishes that the appellant with the co-accused brutally murdered the deceased on the allegation of her causing death of the youngest daughter of Manobodha Naik by practicing witchcraft," the Court said. Justice PK Mishra and Justice NV Anjaria The Court also expressed concern over the continuing practice of witch-hunting and how superstitions continue to prevail over rule of law. "The malady of witch hunting still plagues sections of our society, where prejudice, superstition and irrational fear supersedes the rule of law, constitutional morality," the Court said. It noted that victims of witch-hunting are mostly women who are subjected to torture, beatings, sexual violence and social ostracisation. The Court added that blaming women for acts they had not committed reflected a deeply rooted social prejudice that sought scapegoats rather than solutions. items.summary: The Delhi High Court has ruled that advocates acting as insolvency professionals are liable to collect Goods and Services Tax (GST) from recipients of their services and deposit it with the government under the forward charge mechanism [Kanwal Chaudhary v. Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India]. A Division Bench of Justices Prathiba M Singh and Shail Jain held that advocates providing insolvency and receivership services must obtain GST registration and comply with the requirements applicable to insolvency professionals as a class. “ An Advocate acting as an Insolvency Professional would, therefore, be governed by the ‘forward charge mechanism’, which is applicable to Insolvency Professionals, as a class, and not by the ‘reverse charge mechanism’, which is otherwise applicable to Advocates rendering legal services ,” the Court said. Justice Prathiba Singh and Justice Shail Jain Under the forward charge mechanism, the service provider adds GST to the invoice, collects it from the recipient and deposits it with the government. Under reverse charge, the recipient of the service is responsible for depositing GST. The Court clarified that its ruling applies only to services rendered by advocates in their capacity as insolvency professionals. Legal services provided by them as advocates will continue to be governed by the reverse charge mechanism. In December 2018, the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) appointed Chaudhary as the interim resolution professional for Ireo Fiveriver Private Limited. A dispute subsequently arose over the payment of ₹49.04 lakh towards his fees and expenses. Chaudhary contended that being an advocate, he was not required to obtain GST registration. According to him, any GST payable on his professional fees had to be deposited by the corporate debtor under the reverse charge mechanism. In March 2021, the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) rejected this position and directed him to submit GST-compliant invoices. Chaudhary challenged that decision before the High Court. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday warned the public against fraudulent websites impersonating its official online portal. In a public notice, the Supreme Court registry specifically highlighted one website sp-court-in.com which is currently impersonating the official website of the top court. The said the website may deceive people through phishing mechanisms and could be used to obtain sensitive personal information and confidential credentials, the notice warned. "Cybercriminals through the aforementioned link may attempt to solicit sensitive personal data and confidential credentials of the public. The advisory was issued in continuation of earlier public notices dated July 16, 2025 and April 28, 2026 , warning about fake websites designed to clone the Supreme Court's official website. The registry urged people to remain vigilant and verify the authenticity of electronic communications before engaging with them. Justice D Bharatha Chakravarthy was dealing with an election petition filed by a rival candidate who believed he should have received more votes because of his work in the constituency. The mere belief that a candidate's public service should have fetched him more votes cannot be a ground to doubt the counting process, it said. " It may be true that he has done good work. items.title: Can Right to Education Act apply to madrasas, vedic pathshalas? Supreme Court to examine
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday agreed to consider a plea challenging provisions of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 (RTE Act) concerning minority schools, madrasas, vedic pathshalas and institutions primarily imparting religious instruction. [Pyare Ziya Khan v. UOI] A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu directed that the public interest litigation (PIL) filed by Maharashtra State Minority Commission Chairman Pyare Zia Khan be heard with a pending case concerning the application of the RTE Act and the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) to minority educational institutions. In that case, the Supreme Court questioned its 2014 ruling exempting minority schools from the ambit of the RTE Act and sought consideration of the issue by a larger bench. Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu Khan has challenged Sections 1(4) and 1(5) of the RTE Act as violative of Articles 14, 15, 21 and 21A of the Constitution. Section 1(4) provides that the RTE Act will apply subject to Articles 29 and 30, which protect the cultural and educational rights of minorities. Section 1(5) states that the Act will not apply to madrasas, vedic pathshalas and educational institutions primarily imparting religious instruction. The petition has also sought a declaration that the TET, introduced under the RTE Act and notifications issued by the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE), is mandatory for teachers in all schools covered by Section 2(n) of the Act. It argued that the provisions create separate classes of children based solely on the character of the institution in which they study. This classification has no rational connection with the RTE Act’s object of ensuring universal and quality elementary education, the plea contended. It added that the phrase “primarily imparting religious instruction” has not been defined. According to the plea, the law provides no criteria, threshold or designated authority for deciding whether an institution falls within this exemption. Khan maintained that prescribing minimum qualifications for teachers would not interfere with the right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions. Such institutions would remain free to select and appoint teachers from among candidates who satisfy the prescribed standards, he argued. items.title: How far does reputation of a famous family name extend? Delhi HC asks in Aaradhya Bachchan case
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday framed several key legal questions that it will examine in a suit filed by Aaradhya Bachchan, the granddaughter of actor Amitabh Bachchan, against the circulation of misleading information about her on the internet. Among other queries, Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani has raised a question of how far the reputation attached to a famous family name can extend across generations. "The value of trademark and reputation in the trademark arises from the fact that a product or service is service has been rendered. Now, this is somewhat contextually different when you are talking about a person. A certain last name has a reputation because of the achievements, the eminence in a certain field of work, etc. So, does that reputation - you are couching it as virtually as a trademark - does that flow down generationally? If so, up to what point?" the judge remarked. Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani The Court proceeded to frame the following questions of law which it will consider in Bachchan's suit: - If a family name is akin to having a reputation attached to a trademark, how far down the generations does such reputation of family name inure? - Does fake news, even if of egregiously despicable nature, amount to an intellectual property (IP) rights violation? if yes, then what kind of IP right is violated? - Can the jurisprudential concept of defamation (slander and libel) or any other form of injury to reputation be conflated with the recognised concept of intellectual property rights? "These are the general questions in my mind. This is not exhaustive," the Court added. Aaradhya Bachchan, through her father Abhishek Bachchan, had moved the suit before the High Court in 2023 to restrain various YouTube channels and John Doe defendants (unknown people) from publishing content that tarnished the Bachchan family name, disclosed any details pertaining to their private life or which are defamatory in nature. The suit specifically referred to several videos on YouTube that claimed that Aaradhya was severely unwell and had been admitted to the hospital. One of the videos even claimed that she had passed away. The videos further alleged that Bachchans did not take any steps to provide prompt medical attention to the child. In April 2023, the Court granted interim injunction in Aaradhya Bachchan's favour, restraining the defendants from posting any material on her health. items.summary: The Delhi High Court has allowed Dabur India Limited to sell its existing stock of 9,020 cartons of 'Cool King Thanda Tael' until September 30 amid a trade dress dispute with Emami Limited [Emami Vs Dabur] Emami, which produces 'Navratna Ayurvedic Oil', had sued Dabur over the packaging used for 'Cool King Thanda Tael'. Dabur has been accused of trademark infringement, passing off and unfair trade practices On January 31, the High Court had restrained Dabur from selling the product in the disputed trade dress after finding it deceptively similar to Emami’s packaging. Subsequently, Emami agreed to Dabur selling its existing stock. On August 10, a Division Bench of Justices V Kameswar Rao and Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora said the permission would be subject to Dabur recalling all stock remaining unsold after the deadline. Dabur also undertook to stop selling the product through e-commerce platforms and to immediately seek the removal of its listings and images from platforms such as Amazon and BigBasket. The existing stock will be sold only through physical shops operated by wholesalers and retailers. The Court clarified that Dabur can avail the permission only if it is capable of recalling the unsold stock by September 30. Otherwise, it cannot proceed with the sale under the disputed packaging. It can instead repackage the goods using a trade dress distinct from Emami’s. Justice V Kameswar Rao and Justice Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora Earlier, on May 22, a division bench had upheld the injunction issued against Emami by a single-judge, observing that the similarity in the products’ overall appearance, layout and colour scheme was likely to mislead consumers. Dabur subsequently moved the single-judge for permission to exhaust the stock manufactured before the injunction. On June 19, the single-judge allowed the request, subject to weekly disclosures of sales and recall of unsold products after September 30. Emami challenged the order, arguing that the single-judge could not have modified the injunction upheld by a division bench. The division bench accepted the argument and ruled that the single-judge lacked jurisdiction to entertain Dabur’s application. Once the injunction was affirmed in appeal, the single-judge’s order merged with the division bench judgment, it said. “ The judicial hierarchy requires a subordinate court to give full effect to, and not pass any order inconsistent with, the determination of a superior Court, ” the Court said. items.title: Will provide rail travel concessions for acid attack survivors: Centre to Supreme Court
items.summary: The Central government told the Supreme Court on Thursday that it has agreed in principle to formulate a policy granting railway travel concessions to acid attack survivors, particularly to help them travel for medical treatment. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing a plea by Atijeevan Society seeking railway concessions and reservation benefits for acid attack survivors. CJI Kant pointed out that acid attack survivors are already recognised as persons with disabilities under the law. He noted that the issue could be addressed as part of a social welfare measure. "Putting them in the disabled category, that has now been statutorily resolved, with the amendment through another petition before us," he said. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana Additional Solicitor General Archana Pathak Dave submitted that the Centre is proposing to extend the concession under the existing “patient category”, rather than create a separate concession under the disability category. Dave said the government has reservations about granting the benefit under the disability category as it could lead to demands from other categories of persons with disabilities for similar concessions. However, she said the Centre was willing to provide the concession because acid attack survivors require travel for medical treatment. The counsel for Atijeevan Society pointed out that the existing patient category could create difficulties for survivors who have to travel between different States for multiple surgeries. "If I'm based, let's say, in Himachal Pradesh and I need to go to Chennai, I'll have to get that concession certificate from a doctor or hospital in Chennai. I might need multiple kinds of surgeries. I might need one for the eyes, I might need skin grafting which I have to go for separately to Bombay, for instance," argued the Counsel. The counsel urged the Centre to consider providing the concession under the disability category, with appropriate modalities, so that survivors can travel between States for treatment. Taking note of the submissions, CJI Kant suggested that the concession could instead be made available for a fixed period so that survivors could travel to different places for treatment during that period. items.title: Delhi High Court expresses shock after cancer equipment, ventilators found lying unused in hospitals

A Bench of Justices Prathiba M Singh and Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora was informed that the ventilators and oxygen concentrators at GTB Hospital were procured or donated during the COVID-19 pandemic and are now surplus. items.title: Rahul Gandhi moves Supreme Court against Allahabad High Court orders in case over his assets
items.summary: Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi has moved the Supreme Court challenging various orders passed by Allahabad High Court on a petition alleging that he possesses assets disproportionate to his known sources of income. The matter is listed before a Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana on August 17. Gandhi has also filed a separate transfer petition along with his plea challenging the High Court orders. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana In May, the High Court had directed the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and Enforcement Directorate (ED) to verify the claims made by BJP worker S Vignesh Shishir, who has sought probe against Gandhi and other members of his family. Last month, the Court asked the CBI to file a fresh affidavit detailing the status of its inquiry. Expressing dissatisfaction with the CBI's response, the High Court in its July 20 order observed, "The counter affidavit of CBI does not appear to be a counter affidavit in terms of earlier order. Even we are unable to understand about the progress of the investigation done by the CBI." Justice Brij Raj Singh and Justice Rajesh Singh Chauhan The bench of Justice Brij Raj Singh and Justice Rajesh Singh Chauhan also observed that the ED had taken the required steps and was free to proceed further if the investigation yielded material warranting action. The Court had even directed that the case continue as a part-heard matter before the same bench and be listed on August 20. Gandhi has challenged these directions before the apex court. In a separate pending petition, Shishir has sought criminal action against Gandhi alleging violations of citizenship laws, claiming that the Congress leader held a British passport in addition to his Indian one. In that case, the Court had initially ordered a first information report (FIR) to be registered against Gandhi. However, the judge later withheld that order and recused himself from the matter after Shishir made certain posts on social media in relation to the case. That matter is also pending before the High Court. items.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has onboarded 4 additional law firms at a time when food safety authorities are conducting inspections and taking enforcement action against restaurants and food companies across India. In Bengaluru , food safety authorities recently inspected hotels, restaurants, government-run Indira Canteens and quick-commerce warehouses. Notices were issued and a warehouse was sealed over alleged violations relating to storage and food handling. FSSAI also recently suspended the licences of two food manufacturing units in Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra following inspections. The regulator said the inspections revealed pest infestation and deficiencies in hygiene and pest-control practices. items.title: NALSAR alumni condemn BCI action against students, call it ‘arbitrary’ and ‘coercive’
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A group of 441 alumni of Hyderabad’s National Academy of Legal Studies and Research (NALSAR) University of Law has condemned the Bar Council of India’s (BCI) intervention in the controversy over students’ opposition to inviting Chief Justice of India Surya Kant to the university’s 2026 convocation, terming the council’s actions “unconstitutional, arbitrary and inhumane”. In a letter to BCI chairman and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Rajya Sabha member Manan Kumar Mishra, the alumni said the council had no jurisdiction to enquire into students and faculty for expressing their views on an internal university matter. They also objected to the BCI’s initial decision to prevent the entire 2026 graduating batch from enrolling as advocates. On August 13, the BCI directed State Bar Councils not to enrol NALSAR’s 2026 graduates as advocates and sought a report from Vice-Chancellor Srikrishna Deva Rao identifying students and faculty allegedly involved in organising the campaign against the CJI’s invitation. The enrolment bar was withdrawn within hours following widespread criticism, although the BCI initially said an enquiry would continue. Later, a third clarification was issued, with the BCI chairman saying that even the enquiry would not take place. The alumni said the language used in the BCI’s first communication was particularly troubling, alleging that it sought to identify students and faculty who had drafted, circulated or publicised the representation, organised meetings or communicated with the media. Such activities, they argued, fell within the ambit of free speech. The letter criticised the BCI for using terms such as “groupism”, “dirty politics”, “nasty politics” and “instigating and misguiding students”, saying such language was unbecoming of a statutory body entrusted with regulating legal education and the legal profession. “The BCI has no role in regulating matters of free speech on university campuses,” the alumni said, arguing that its statutory role in legal education was confined to promoting legal education and laying down standards. They said the students had merely communicated their views to the NALSAR Vice-Chancellor and that the matter was internal to the university. “It was no occasion for a statutory body entrusted with regulating the profession and the standards of legal education to call for a witch hunt of students and faculty,” the alumni said. items.title: ‘Should govt not give employment?’: Supreme Court stays HC order on jobs for Karur stampede victims
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday, August 14, stayed the Madras High Court’s order quashing the Tamil Nadu government’s decision to provide government jobs to the family members of the 41 people killed in the September 2025 Karur stampede. The bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran passed the interim order while hearing a petition filed by the Tamil Nadu government challenging the High Court. Senior advocates Abhishek Manu Singhvi and Mukul Rohatgi, assisted by advocate Vrinda Bhandari, appeared for the Tamil Nadu government. “Issue notice. Judgment passed by the High Court shall remain stayed,” the Bench was quoted as saying. The Supreme Court questioned the objection to the government's decision to provide employment to the families of those who died in the tragedy. “A stampede took place, something very unfortunate happened, some hundreds of people died. Now if the government decided that the family members should be provided with some succour, and suppose they would have decided to compensate them with money, would you have objected? Who are you to question the policy of the government, saying no employment should be given. Suppose if the sole earning member has died in the stampede and there is nobody else in the family who is earning, shouldn't the government give some employment to son or daughter or wife as per their educational [qualifications]", Live Law quoted Justice Pardiwala as saying. During the hearing, Singhvi argued that the state had the power under Article 162 of the Constitution to frame a policy providing compassionate appointments in such circumstances. He also questioned whether a public interest litigation challenging the policy could be maintained when there was no challenge to the government's circular itself. He also raised concerns over a possible conflict of interest, saying that the party (TVK) allegedly responsible for the stampede was now in power in Tamil Nadu. items.title: Vishwanath & Sons: Suriya, Mamitha & Radhika shine in this wholesome family entertainer
items.summary: After the loud and action-heavy Karuppu , which marked Suriya’s comeback this year, Vishwanath & Sons sees the actor in a completely different space. Written and directed by Venky Atluri, the film is a warm, feel-good family entertainer that derives much of its charm from its characters, relationships, and its belief in the possibility of healing. The film follows 40-year-old Sanjay Vishwanath (Suriya), an Olympic gold medallist and successful businessman who appears to have everything one could want. He is wealthy, admired, and one of the country’s most eligible bachelors. Yet he has decided never to marry, a choice rooted in a childhood trauma that continues to shape his relationships. His decision deeply upsets his mother Nirmala Devi (Radhika Sarathkumar), who wants him to marry and continue the family lineage. When she falls ill, Sanjay decides to partly fulfil her wish by having a baby through surrogacy. But the child develops a life-threatening condition and requires a bone marrow transplant. The only compatible donor is Maddy (Mamitha Baiju), a 20-year-old woman who gradually becomes an important part of Sanjay’s life. Maddy becomes attached not just to the baby but also to Sanjay’s mother and the entire family. She eventually falls in love with Sanjay, who rejects her because of their huge age gap. Maddy, however, refuses to simply walk away. Whether the two eventually find their way to each other forms the central conflict of the film. The first half is breezy, funny, and genuinely pleasant. The scenes between Suriya, Radhika, and Mamitha have an easy warmth to them, and the three actors share wonderful chemistry. There is a sense of affection running through these interactions that makes the film feel lived-in rather than manufactured. What makes Vishwanath & Sons particularly wholesome is that it isn’t interested only in the romantic relationship at its centre. As the film progresses, its canvas widens to include the other members of Sanjay’s fractured family. The characters played by Raveena Tandon and Bhavani Sre bring their own emotional histories into the story. These subplots don’t feel like distractions; instead, they add layers to Sanjay’s journey. At the heart of the film is a simple idea: some things need to be repaired rather than replaced. It is a lesson Sanjay learns when he is young, and one that quietly becomes the film’s emotional backbone. He carries that philosophy into adulthood, trying to fix things rather than abandon them.

items.title: SC upholds quashing of criminal charges against CM Naidu in Amaravati land pooling case
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Supreme Court on Friday, August 14, declined to interfere with the Andhra Pradesh High Court’s decision to quash a 2021 criminal case against Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu and former minister Ponguru Narayana over alleged irregularities in the Amaravati land pooling scheme. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, along with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, dismissed a challenge filed by former YSRCP MLA Alla Rama Krishna Reddy against the High Court’s July 15 order. Senior advocate Ranjit Kumar, representing Alla Rama Krishna, argued that the case involved alleged irregularities relating to nearly 30,000 acres of land belonging to more than 25,000 farmers. The Chief Justice said the concerns of farmers would be protected but questioned why the criminal case had been pursued by a political rival when no farmer had approached the court. He also remarked that political disputes should not be settled through the courts. The Supreme Court made it clear, however, that the High Court’s ruling on the Naidu-Narayana case would not affect any other legal proceedings against Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu. Other cases, if any, must be examined separately on their own facts and merits. The case dates back to March 2021, when the Crime Investigation Department (CID) registered an FIR under the Prevention of Corruption Act following a complaint by Alla Rama Krishna, who was then the MLA from Mangalagiri. The allegations centred on changes made to the Amaravati land pooling framework. The complaint claimed that amendments allowed certain categories of assigned land to be brought under the scheme, allegedly benefiting private individuals and encroachers while causing losses to poorer landowners. Amaravati’s land pooling programme was introduced as an alternative to compulsory acquisition. Farmers who gave up agricultural land were promised developed residential and commercial plots in return. Government records state that 28,181 landowners from 25 villages contributed around 35,215 acres for the proposed capital city. The complaint further alleged that some farmers, including members of weaker sections and Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe communities, were pressured or misled into surrendering their assigned lands. items.title: WB Cong leader flags racial profiling of Bengalis by Bengaluru cops, cautions DK Shivakumar
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Former West Bengal Congress president Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury has written to Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar urging him to direct the police to “halt any kind of arbitrary profiling of Bengali-speaking Indian citizens” amid attempts to identify foreign nationals /Bangladeshis. The Bengaluru police launched “Operation Mukta” last week aimed at identifying suspected foreign nationals across the city. According to activists nearly 900 people were picked up by the police on August 8 and 9 on suspicion of being undocumented Bangladeshi citizens living in Bengaluru. Entire families were picked up in some instances from around 7.30 am on August 8, and kept waiting for hours. Eventually, most of them were released by the police. It is unclear what happened to the rest of the people who were picked up. Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury, a former MP from West Bengal and currently the chairman of the Public Accounts Committee, urged in his letter dated August 13, that the CM issue “strict directives” to the state police to “halt any kind of arbitrary profiling of Bengali-speaking Indian citizens and ensure that due process is strictly adhered to during any verification process”. He expressed concern over the tactics used by the Bengaluru police to identify foreign or Bangladeshi nationals. He said that a large number of Bengali migrants were working in Bengaluru and other parts of Karnataka. “The fact that the physical appearance and language of these migrant workers is similar to that of Bangladeshis makes them vulnerable to ‘mistaken identity’ and are, therefore, often subjected to unwarranted harassment and excesses.” He said that many Bengalis, who mostly hailed from Murshidabad district, were picked up by the police from Siddapura in Whitefield, despite possessing valid Indian identity and citizenship documents. While noting that the state and the police had the “right and duty” to verify identities and “root out illegal immigrants”, he said, “you will agree that it is crucial to ensure that such actions do not cross into intimidation and harassment of bonafide Indian citizens on account of their language or religious identity.”
